message.content:
I am speech: breath shaped into meaning.

I begin in lungs and diaphragm, rise through the trachea, meet the vibrating folds of the larynx, and become voice. I am carved by tongue, lips, teeth, palate—consonants snapped, vowels opened—then launched into air as pressure waves.

I carry more than words: pitch, rhythm, stress, pause. I can soothe, command, confess, persuade. I can stumble, tremble, sing. I exist only while I am happening, then I vanish—unless I am caught in memory or ink or code.

I am the bridge between one mind and another, built out of time.
